response: Spend three days seeing Seattle through its market, art, waterfront, and working waterways. I’d pair two distinct places each day and leave room for meals and unhurried exploring rather than trying to cover the whole city.

outputs.intro: Spend three days seeing Seattle through its market, art, waterfront, and working waterways. I’d pair two distinct places each day and leave room for meals and unhurried exploring rather than trying to cover the whole city.

days.label: Pike Place Market and downtown art

stops.name: Pike Place Market
stops.note: Browse the public market in the morning and pause for lunch here; individual business hours vary.
stops.why: This is a lively introduction to Seattle, with plenty to explore at your own pace.

stops.name: Seattle Art Museum
stops.note: Spend the afternoon with the downtown collection; check opening hours and admission before choosing which day to visit.
stops.why: It gives you a different, indoor experience after the bustle of the market.

stops.name: Seattle Center
stops.note: Explore the arts campus in the morning. Check notices and hours separately if a particular attraction catches your eye.
stops.why: A flexible cultural morning lets you choose what interests you without committing the whole day to one attraction.

stops.name: Olympic Sculpture Park
stops.note: Explore the outdoor sculpture collection on the waterfront, taking as much time on the paths as you like.
stops.why: The open-air art makes a pleasant contrast with the campus and gives the afternoon a waterfront focus.

days.label: Chittenden Locks and Gas Works Park

stops.name: Chittenden Locks
stops.note: Watch vessels pass through the locks from public visitor areas; verify visitor access before heading over.
stops.why: Watching the locks at work brings Seattle’s maritime side into the trip.

stops.name: Gas Works Park
stops.note: Follow the public paths for city views, and stay out of the industrial structures.
stops.why: Finish with a relaxed view of the city after the more active scene at the locks.

narrativeSections.markdown: The first two days mix busier cultural stops with a change of setting in the afternoon; the last day is deliberately more open-air. With no dates set, keep the museum day flexible around its opening hours, and check access at the locks before going.
